title.value: Designing and Evaluating Dialogue LLMs for Co-Creative Improvised Theatre
title.justification: The title clearly identifies the main focus of the paper: the design and evaluation of dialogue models for improvisational theatre.
title.quote: Designing and Evaluating Dialogue LLMs for Co-Creative Improvised Theatre

analysis.description: The research paper explores the deployment and evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs) in performing arts, specifically in co-creative improvised theatre, highlighting the technical and interactive challenges faced during live performances at the 2023 Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

type.justification: The paper describes a live deployment of LLMs in a real-world setting (Edinburgh Festival Fringe) and involves the collection of audience and actor feedback, making it an empirical study.
type.quote: This case study investigates human improvisers co-creating with conversational agents in a professional theatre setting.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the use of conversational Large Language Models (LLMs) in theatre, which aligns with the field of conversational AI.
name.quote: Our study was formed in response to the recent advancements in natural language computing and conversational AI which have highlighted the potential of ubiquitous AI participating in human social and creative lives.

name.justification: The use of Large Language Models (LLMs) involves processing and generating natural language, which is a core aspect of NLP.
name.quote: We deployed a conversational agent powered by three different Large Language Models (LLMs) to improvise with a company of professional actors.

name.justification: Chat GPT 3.5 is specifically mentioned as one of the models used in the theatre performances.

is_contributed.justification: Chat GPT 3.5 was used in the study but it was not developed by the authors.
is_contributed.quote: We deployed a conversational agent powered by three different Large Language Models (LLMs).

is_executed.justification: The model was actively used in live performances at the festival, indicating it was executed as part of the study.
is_executed.quote: We deployed a conversational agent powered by three different Large Language Models (LLMs) to improvise.

is_compared.justification: The model was used alongside other models, suggesting a form of comparison, as indicated in the audience and actor feedback analysis.
is_compared.quote: LLMs were generating different numbers of lines... we noticed that each LLM had, overally, a comparable chance of being selected by the curator.
